_doc: AUTHORED reading of Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 28 for the background behind Prairie Avenue: Calumet Avenue's west frontage, 18th to 20th Street (T-3008, piece 1 of T-2983, which tools/census_prairie_1904_background.py ranks the most-seen block face off the avenue). The T-1841 census (chicago/prairie_1904_v1/data/sheet_census/sheet-28.json) counts Prairie frontages only, so these nine rows are read here, in the same frontage contract, for tools/trace_prairie_1904_footprints.py (sheet '28x') and tools/draft_prairie_1904.py. 1800 Calumet is not here: its two glasshouse ranges and lodge are Pullman's estate across 18th Street, allocated by the sheet-28 census to T-1934 (s28-pullman-service-garden).

reading.by: Read by eye from the committed sheet 28 scan (5873 x 7323 px) at 1x and 0.5x over the Calumet lots, 2026-10-22.
reading.conventions: Sanborn colour: pink brick, yellow frame, blue stone. A crossed square marks a stable. D = dwelling. Storey figures as printed (B = basement).
reading.limits: A 1911 label is a 1911 observation (study ruling 11): the one 'GARAGE' is backcast as a stable. Robinson 1886 plate 10 ends north of 1830, so no earlier plan checks these outlines. No dimension is claimed beyond the trace.

polygons.reading_1911: 2B brick dwelling (D) with a rounded bay at the south corner of its Calumet front and a 2B rear part behind a dashed line; a one-storey and a two-storey frame closet (T.CL.) on its north side at the alley end

frontages.why: No named record or 1904 directory row for this lot is in the T-1837 study, and Robinson 1886 plate 10 stops north of it, so the 1911 sheet is the only plan: the draft stands the sheet's house for 1904 as background, its presence inferred from the sheet alone (study ruling 11) under the block's single liberty.
